-            for k in where.pop(pair, ()):

-                if len(new) == len(old):

-                ids[k] = new

+                cands = set(compress(stats, map(top.__eq__, vals)))
+                # first candidate in chunk order, then position order (scan in C)
+                pair = next(filter(cands.__contains__,
+                                   chain.from_iterable(map(zip, ids, map(_tail, ids)))))
+                top = stats[pair]
+            # mint a new token: assign it the next available id
+            idx = 256 + i
+            # replace all occurrences of pair in the chunks that hold both
+            # tokens; the pair count differences are accumulated (dec: pairs
+            # of the old chunks, inc: pairs of the new chunks) and applied once
+            dec = {}
+            inc = {}
+            dec_get = dec.get
+            inc_get = inc.get
+            # a merged pair never reappears, so its chunk set can be dropped
+            for k in where.pop(pair, ()):
+                old = ids[k]
+                new = merge(old, pair, idx)
+                n = len(new)
+                m = len(old) - n # number of merged occurrences
+                if not m:
+                    continue
+                ids[k] = new
+                w = weights[k]
+                if w == 1:
+                    _count_elements(dec, zip(old, old[1:]))
+                    _count_elements(inc, zip(new, new[1:]))
+                else:
+                    for p in zip(old, old[1:]):
+                        dec[p] = dec_get(p, 0) + w
+                    for p in zip(new, new[1:]):
+                        inc[p] = inc_get(p, 0) + w
+                # only pairs containing idx are new to this chunk; every other
+                # pair of new was already a pair of old (so k is in where[p])
+                index = new.index
+                q = -1
+                for _ in range(m):
+                    q = index(idx, q + 1)
+                    if q:
+                        where[(new[q-1], idx)].add(k)
+                    if q + 1 < n:
+                        where[(idx, new[q+1])].add(k)
+            for p, c in dec.items():
+                stats[p] -= c
+            for p, c in inc.items():
+                stats[p] = stats_get(p, 0) + c
+            for p in dec:
+                if stats_get(p) == 0:
+                    del stats[p]
